label: Aristotle, Physics III.3, 202a13-16: MOTION_2 is in the moved: whenever something moves a thing in…
interpretation: Typed reading in the act/potency vocabulary of beings and respects: whenever something moves a thing in a respect, that thing is being moved in that respect. Motion is in the movable because it is the movable's actuality, brought about by what can move it (202a13-14), and the mover's actuality is not another (202a15-16). The -A reading keeps the occurrence-level form (a motion is in its movable); this one speaks of beings and respects and says nothing about motions as objects. It adds no claim about the mover's own motion. Scope: Aristotle's physical motion; the Lean has no guard, so the reading is accepted only under a physical instantiation of `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` (DISAMB-MOTION).
